policy.retrieval_rule: Freeze resolved URL, byte count, SHA-256 checksum, retrieval time, and terms before analysis.

sources.assay: 10x single-cell RNA-seq of mobilized CD34-positive HSPCs
sources.format: donor-separated 10x feature-barcode matrices in ZIP archives
sources.citation: Severe inflammation and lineage skewing is associated with poor engraftment of engineered hematopoietic stem cells in patients with sickle cell disease. Nature Communications (2025). doi:10.1038/s41467-025-58321-4
verified: All six donor archives resolve without authentication.
The archives contain unfiltered feature-barcode matrices, so cell calling is required.
limitations: SCD HSPCs were collected in a mobilization and gene-therapy context.
Cross-sectional RNA profiles do not observe cell fate.
Exact asset checksums remain to be frozen at retrieval.

sources.assay: 10x single-cell RNA-seq of bone-marrow CD34-positive cells
sources.comparison: 4 healthy donors and 5 SCD donors; 3 thalassemia donors and 1 lineage-depleted healthy sample excluded
sources.format: GEO supplementary TAR of donor-level processed matrices
sources.license: NCBI GEO public repository terms; source attribution required
sources.citation: Hua et al. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of human bone marrow reveals molecular features of hematopoietic stem cells in sickle cell disease. Blood (2020). doi:10.1182/blood.2019002301
verified: GEO reports public status, donor groups, raw SRA availability, and a processed supplementary archive.
The processed archive resolves without authentication.
limitations: The cohort is small and differs from the discovery collection context.
Thalassemia and lineage-depleted samples are outside the v1 comparison.
Cross-sectional RNA profiles do not observe cell fate.

sources.assay: bulk RNA-seq of sorted CD45-positive lineage-negative CD34-positive CD38-negative bone-marrow HSPCs
sources.comparison: reported 4 non-SCD controls and 7 SCD individuals
sources.license: NCBI GEO public repository terms; source attribution required
sources.citation: Premature senescence impairs hematopoietic stem cell function during sickle cell disease in mice and humans. GEO GSE277682
verified: The processed count matrix resolves without authentication.
limitations: Bulk RNA-seq cannot estimate cell-state fate probabilities.
Use is restricted to orthogonal lineage, stemness, or senescence program direction.
Participant metadata require re-verification at retrieval because the release is recent.

sources.assay: CITE-seq of c-Kit-enriched Townes-model bone-marrow HSPCs
sources.comparison: AA and SS mice at 2 and 6 months with 4 biological replicates per condition and age
sources.format: GEX count archive and ADT count matrix
sources.license: NCBI GEO public repository terms; source attribution required
sources.citation: Premature senescence impairs hematopoietic stem cell function during sickle cell disease in mice and humans. GEO GSE277681
verified: Processed GEX and ADT assets resolve without authentication.
limitations: This is a mouse disease model, not human evidence.
Age is confounded with processing batch, so age effects are not independently estimable.
Use is restricted to within-age disease-direction support.

sources.assay: longitudinal somatic-mutation clonal tracking after gene therapy
sources.comparison: SCD participants before and after gene therapy; no healthy comparator
sources.format: controlled raw sequencing and publicly viewable derived files
sources.license: No explicit license found for the author-derived repository; raw sequencing is controlled
sources.citation: Clonal selection of hematopoietic stem cells after gene therapy for sickle cell disease. Nature Medicine (2023). doi:10.1038/s41591-023-02636-6
verified: The paper describes longitudinal clone tracking.
limitations: Institutional controlled-data access violates the zero-budget open-data boundary.
No healthy comparison answers the v1 estimand.
The public derived repository has no explicit reuse license.
sources.exclusion_reason: Not an open, licensed, healthy-versus-SCA input for v1; retain only as a future methodological pointer.
